diseases.guidance: Boil every litre that passes a lip. Purified stores block the water route entirely. The first cramps are just the beginning—then comes the purging.
diseases.source_note: Shared cisterns and ration lines were the old strain's best friend. It lives in what we drink, not in us. The water tastes faintly of copper and decay before the symptoms even begin.
diseases.tell: rice-water stool within a day of drinking
diseases.tell_secondary: vomiting, then cramps that will not let go
diseases.timing_clue: hours after a shared water source; the whole intake line falls first

diseases.guidance: Seal the vents and keep masks on shift hands. Air moves faster than rumor does. The cough starts as a tickle, then becomes a rasp that sounds like grinding teeth.
diseases.source_note: Carried in from scavenged bedding and dead livestock. It jumps mouths before it jumps fences. The fever burns away memories first—then the body.
diseases.tell: abrupt fever with dry cough and aching
diseases.tell_secondary: sore throat first, then chest tightness
diseases.timing_clue: one day after crowded animal contact

diseases.guidance: Sterilise every tool before it touches skin. One reused blade can seed a ward. The fever starts with a chill that feels like ice water in the veins.
diseases.source_note: Spread through unsterilised surgical tools and shared field dressings. The worst cases die with clean hands nearby. The blood never washes clean—only diluted.
diseases.tell: fever with ache behind the eyes and at the wounds
diseases.timing_clue: days after shared needles or unwashed tools

diseases.guidance: Engage air filtration and keep sealed kit on anyone who peeled mold off the walls. Spores live longer than patience. The first cough brings up black flecks that look like ash but aren't.
diseases.source_note: A grey bloom that rode the dust down from the dead farms. It does not need a wound, only a breath. The lungs fill with grey filaments before the patient even knows they're sick.
diseases.tell: fever with a spreading grey rash
diseases.timing_clue: a few days after working spore-heavy ground unsealed

diseases.guidance: Take iodine immediately. Then pray. The vomiting starts with clear fluid, then becomes bloody. The skin burns from the inside out.
diseases.source_note: The silent killer. No cough, no fever—just the slow unraveling of the body's ability to heal itself. The first sign is often the refusal to eat.
diseases.tell: vomiting within a day of heavy exposure, then a false calm
diseases.tell_secondary: reddened skin, gums bleeding, hair loosening
diseases.timing_clue: hours to a day of onset marks the dose; the calm before day five fools everyone

diseases.guidance: The spores are in the air you breathe. The cough starts dry, then produces thick yellow mucus that clogs the lungs. The fever never breaks.
diseases.source_note: Thrives in damp, dark places where the air doesn't circulate. The bunker's ventilation system is both its enemy and its highway.
diseases.timing_clue: slow — a fortnight after dust exposure

diseases.guidance: Boil all water for at least five minutes. The diarrhea starts watery, then becomes bloody. The fever rises steadily, day by day, until the mind begins to wander.
diseases.source_note: The classic killer of crowded spaces. The bunker's water purification system is the only thing standing between you and the grave. The taste of the water changes before the symptoms do.
diseases.tell: sustained fever that will not break by morning
diseases.tell_secondary: rose spots on the belly, dull headache
diseases.timing_clue: days after the water, not hours — it sneaks

diseases.guidance: Boil every litre that passes a lip. The cramp arrives like a fist under the ribs, then comes the watery purging. Most who rest and rehydrate walk it off. The young and the old do not.
diseases.source_note: Coastal-well strain that rode in on the flood surge. It lives in the cistern and on the ladle handle, not in the patient. Three-phase tell: the nausea comes first, the cramps second, the relapse fever third. Half the ward recovers without treatment if the water source is cut.
diseases.tell: griping diarrhoea, no fever to speak of
diseases.tell_secondary: flatulence and cramping after drawing water

diseases.guidance: Cap every well and bleed silt out before anybody drinks. The yellowing starts in the eyes, then the skin. By the time the urine turns the colour of dark tea, the kidneys are already half gone.
diseases.source_note: Rodent-borne spirochete that colonised the lower wells after the floodplain drained back. Person-to-person spread is rare; the well is the patient. Three-phase tell: a hard flu ten days in, then jaundice on day fourteen, then renal collapse on day twenty. Untreated, the case fatality is brutal. Pairs with cholera as the second tier of waterborne aftermath.
diseases.tell: yellow in the eyes before the skin
diseases.timing_clue: a week or more after flood-water contact

diseases.guidance: Masks on anyone working the dead barns. The cough has no sound for the first week, then it sounds like glass in the lungs. Three-phase tell: a heavy night-sweat, then a dry cough, then a wet one that breaks the fever or breaks the patient.
diseases.source_note: Aerosol from livestock carcasses left to rot in the closed-by barns. It does not need a wound, only a breath. The first wave arrives nine to fourteen days after the carcass is opened; the second wave carries far on the wind. Three-phase tell: first a heavy night-sweat, the second sign is a dry cough, and the third is a wet one that breaks the fever or the patient. Pairs with zoonotic flu but slower to start and harder to shake.
diseases.tell: tight cough with breathlessness on the stairs
diseases.tell_secondary: low fever that worsens in the sealed rooms
diseases.timing_clue: days, worse for those who sleep below the vents

diseases.guidance: Mask every shift and crack a vent. The hiss is not a wheeze, it is the sound of a chest that will not empty. Three-phase tell: a cold that does not move, a cough that does not wet, a chest that does not clear. Most recover at rest; some do not.
diseases.source_note: An atypical pneumonia that thrives in cold, dry, recirculated air. It rides the room, not the wind. Three-phase tell: first night-sweats, the second sign is a cough that tastes like copper, and the third is a fever that will not break. The most common cause of a fifty-bed ward losing a quarter of its shift to a single week of coughing. Pairs with fungal respiratory as the chronic cousin; this comes on faster and leaves faster.
diseases.tell: dry hacking cough, no phlegm at all
diseases.tell_secondary: hoarseness and a headache that lifts outdoors
diseases.timing_clue: weeks of unfiltered air; improves on surface duty

diseases.guidance: Clean every scratch before it closes. The wound looks fine on day one and angry on day three. By day five the patient is shaking in the bed. Sterilise the dressing, sterilise the blade, sterilise the hand.
diseases.source_note: Gram-positive sepsis seeded by dirty iron wounds — rebar, tin sheeting, rusted car-door edges. Three-phase tell: a hot and angry red line on day two, a shaking chill on day three, a clouded mind on day five. Always kills through the wound, never through the air.
diseases.tell: red streaking out from an unhealing wound
diseases.tell_secondary: fever that spikes in the evening; the dressing smells
diseases.timing_clue: two or three days after a rust-wound, on the limb it entered

diseases.guidance: One needle, one patient, one draw. Sharing the syringe shares the ward. The rash starts on the forearms, climbs to the chest, and stops only when the antibiotics start. Three-phase tell: a hot vein on day one, a creeping rash on day two, a fever that does not break on day three.
diseases.source_note: Gram-positive infection spread by field-side needle reuse: vaccinations, blood draws, IV lines. Less lethal than septic rust but faster moving. Carries the moral weight of the choice to share — the ward remembers who kept their kit separate. Three-phase tell: first a hot vein on day one, the second sign is a creeping rash on day two, and the third is a fever that will not break on day three.
diseases.tell: fever with flank pain after an injection
diseases.tell_secondary: the injection site is warm, but looks clean
diseases.timing_clue: days after a needle was reused, wherever it went in

diseases.guidance: Full kit on every digger from day one. The spores come up with the dirt and stay up for a week. Three-phase tell: a chest cold on day six, blood in the sputum on day twelve, weight loss by the pound on day sixteen. The patient survives or does not.
diseases.source_note: Invasive mold that colonises silt-rich substrate opened by deep excavation. Pairs with spore blight as the chronic cousin; this one is faster to seed and harder to displace. Three-phase tell: first a chest cold on day six, the second sign is blood in the sputum on day twelve, and the third is weight loss by the pound on day sixteen. Until the host schedules a dig-arrival event, this disease floats in the master spread pool and drifts in randomly on any roster with a digger.
diseases.tell: breathlessness with a sweet, earthy smell on the breath
diseases.tell_secondary: chest pain on deep breath; black specks in sputum
diseases.timing_clue: late — a week past the dig, and only for those who went down

diseases.guidance: Hoods on, vents cracked, and never sleep inside a sealed silo. The whisper-cough arrives a week after the exposure, and it never fully leaves. Three-phase tell: a hard breath at the top of the stairs on day nine, a wheeze at night on day twelve, a chest cold that returns every harvest.
diseases.source_note: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis from compacted grain-spore aerosol. It is not the spores themselves but the immune reaction to them. Commonest among longtime bunker-farmers. Three-phase tell: first a hard breath at the top of the stairs on day nine, the second sign is a wheeze at night on day twelve, and the third is a chest cold that returns every harvest. Pairs with fungal respiratory — patients with one rarely get the other; once the immune system bets wrong, it stops betting again.
diseases.tell: cough that worsens some hours after dust, not during
diseases.tell_secondary: tightness and fever after clean-out work
diseases.timing_clue: half a day to two days after silo or grain dust

vector_protocols.note: Boiled or treated water goes stale in a shared cistern; it is re-done on the rota.
Work details open the vents within days; the seal never survives a shift change.
Sterile stock lasts, but every dressing and blade spends it.
Filters clog. Swap them or the blower pushes spores deeper.
